mean_slope.text: Predict mean slope <= .5 (undefined for zero occupancy, no pseudocount).

hierarchy.text: Hierarchy should produce unequal head peaks.
hierarchy.verdict: unequal at and past 2048; at T512 heads 1-3 tie at 256

slopes_block_invariance: heads 1-3 slopes are identical across all six blocks; head 0 slope is 8.6e-17 in blocks 0-3 and 0.0046/0.0045 in blocks 4-5 (peak 62-64 of 64 everywhere).

capacity_and_pressure.caveat: Registered caveat: budget-capped occupancy alone is not evidence of semantic compression. Heads 2/3 reach their budgets and refuse writes (R-CAP) by T2048/T4096; the sublinear slopes are substantially capacity-forced.

x39_semantic_reference.note: X39 semantic arm: one four-head lane, slope mean 0.108. The v1 pure six-block stack is deeper-sloped (0.254) but the deep lanes are budget-capped, unlike the uncapped semantic arm.

compression_answer: The six-lane stack compresses in the occupancy-vs-length sense: mean log-log slope 0.2539 (16x tokens -> 5.75x peak on the deepest lane), every lane sublinear, fast lane flat at its 64-slot budget from T512 on. Ordering follows the horizon constants past training length: peaks at T8192 are [64, 256, 736, 1472] = strictly increasing with horizon. This is capacity+decay ordering, not learned semantic compression; the always-enable diagnostic removes selective-write evidence.
